description: Transmission Control Protocol - Reliable, connection-oriented OSI Layer 4 protocol using three-way handshakes.
User Datagram Protocol - Lightweight, connectionless OSI Layer 4 transport protocol prioritizing speed over reliability.
Internet Protocol - Principal Layer 3 network protocol responsible for routing packets across network boundaries.
Internet Protocol version 4 - 32-bit connectionless IP addressing scheme yielding ~4.3 billion addresses.
Internet Protocol version 6 - 128-bit hexadecimal addressing format designed to replace exhausted IPv4 space.
Internet Control Message Protocol - Network Layer diagnostic protocol used for network utility commands like PING.
Address Resolution Protocol - Protocol resolving Layer 3 IP addresses to Layer 2 physical MAC hardware addresses.
Domain Name System - Hierarchical protocol resolving human-friendly domain names to numeric IP addresses.
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol - Network service automatically assigning IP addresses and subnet parameters.
Network Address Translation - Process remapping private internal IP addresses to a public IP address.
Port Address Translation - Variant of NAT mapping multiple private IPs to a single public IP via unique port numbers.
Virtual Local Area Network - Logical grouping of network devices isolated into separate broadcast domains on switches.
Virtual Private Network - Encrypted tunnel extending a private network securely across a public network.
Local Area Network - Network interconnecting computers within a limited geographic area like an office building.
Wide Area Network - Telecommunications network spanning large geographical distances between sites.
Wireless Local Area Network - Local area network using high-frequency radio waves to communicate.
Metropolitan Area Network - Interconnected computer network spanning an entire city or campus geography.
Network Interface Card - Hardware component connecting a computer host to a computer network.
Media Access Control - Unique 48-bit physical hardware address assigned to a NIC for Layer 2 communications.
Maximum Transmission Unit - Largest protocol data unit size in bytes that can be transmitted across a network layer.
Classless Inter-Domain Routing - Standardized method for allocating IP addresses and routing packets using network prefixes.
Border Gateway Protocol - Core routing protocol of the internet exchanging routing information between Autonomous Systems.
Open Shortest Path First - Interior gateway link-state routing protocol finding the shortest path for IP packets.
Routing Information Protocol - Distance-vector routing protocol using hop count as a routing metric.
Spanning Tree Protocol - Layer 2 network protocol preventing bridge loops in redundant network topologies.
Quality of Service - Control features prioritizing specific critical network traffic over less urgent data queues.
Software-Defined Networking - Architecture decoupling network control logic from physical data forwarding hardware.
Software-Defined Wide Area Network - Architecture managing WAN connections dynamically using software control logic.
